correctness.rationale: If σ is a nonclique closed-neighborhood face, a nonadjacent pair x,y in σ has a witnessing center v. v is unique because two common neighbors would create a C4; v is different from x,y and σ\{v} is still nonclique. Pair every nonclique face τ missing its center with τ∪{v}; order lower members by decreasing cardinality. Every other coface of τ is a larger nonclique face with the same center and has already been removed, giving a genuine free-face elementary collapse. Center/cardinality are canonical, so whole stages are automorphism invariant. C4-freeness forbids K4 and edge-sharing graph triangles; choose one private edge of each triangle and collapse the clique complex to a graph with e-t edges and c components (this later choice need not be equivariant). Graph cycle lattice modulo independent signed triangle boundaries yields 0→Z[oriented triangles]→H1(G,Z)→H1(N[G],Z)→0; private edge supports make this sublattice primitive and quotient torsion-free. C4 is sharp: N[C4]=∂Δ3 but clique complex is a circle. Independent exhaustive simple-graph checks for n<=5: C4-free counts 1,2,8,54,548 and all canonical free pairs replayed correctly.
